column1: # LongMemEval-S question set — N=40 stratified CI-ratchet manifest.
# Column 1 = zero-based offset into the longmemeval_s dataset (the value
# passed as LUNARIS_EVAL_LME_OFFSET). Column 2 = the dataset's question
# category.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS
# The ratchet ran on offsets16.tsv, which has two defects that together
# made the gate incapable of failing on anything short of a catastrophe:
#   1. SENSITIVITY. At N=16 with tolerance 1, the fail floor is 14/16 —
#      the gate only trips on a drop of 2 questions, i.e. ~12.5 points of
#      retrieval. A 5-point regression passes silently.
#   2. COVERAGE. offsets16.tsv contains only `multi-session` and
#      `single-session-preference`. Four of the six LongMemEval-S
#      categories — including `temporal-reasoning` (26% of the N=125
#      manifest) and `knowledge-update` — were not measured AT ALL, so a
#      regression confined to one of them was invisible at any N.
# At N=40 with tolerance 1 the gate trips on a 2-question drop = exactly
# 5.0 points, which is the stated sensitivity target, and all six
# categories are present. See scripts/bench/lme/baselines/README.md for
# the full arithmetic and the runner-cost tradeoff.
# Category mix (largest-remainder proportional to offsets125.tsv's
# 33/33/19/18/14/8): 11 multi-session, 11 temporal-reasoning,
# 6 knowledge-update, 6 single-session-user, 4 single-session-assistant,
# 2 single-session-preference.
# DERIVATION (deterministic, reproducible, no sampling)
# Rows are a subset of offsets125.tsv. Within each category the k rows
# are taken at evenly-spaced source indices `offs[round(i*m/k)]` for
# i in 0..k-1, where m is that category's row count in offsets125.tsv.
# No RNG, no seed, no cherry-picking: re-deriving from offsets125.tsv
# reproduces this file byte for byte.
# Changing this file changes what "N=40" means and INVALIDATES the
# checked-in baseline (tally.py refuses on a total mismatch, exit 6).
# Add a new file rather than editing this one.
